transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’m having a hard time with eating. It’s kind of embarrassing to say, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but sometimes once I start eating, it feels like I sort of… disappear, or like something else takes over. Even while I’m telling myself to stop, I just keep going until I really can’t stand it anymore.
Do you ever feel like you've eaten an amount of food that's definitely larger than what most people would eat in a similar time period?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I try not to think of it that way, but there have been nights after studying where I’ll eat dinner at the dining hall and then go back to my room and keep eating—like burgers, cereal, peanut butter, snacks, just whatever I can get.

It ends up being… a lot more than a normal dinner, I guess. Like the trash is full afterward and I feel really sick. I know that probably sounds bad.
How do you feel about yourself after one of these eating episodes?

Pretty awful, honestly… but I try not to make a big deal out of it. It’s like, even if the day was okay — like I went to class and handled things — afterward I’ll catch my reflection in a dorm window or something and just think my stomach or my face looks bigger than the guys around me.

And then it feels like I failed at everything, not just eating. I just want to hide so nobody has to look at me. I know that probably sounds kind of dramatic, but that’s where my head goes.
Do you ever try to get rid of the extra calories after one of these eating episodes?

Um… yeah. I mean, I don’t like saying that, but… after I eat like that, I usually end up trying to make myself throw up.

Sometimes I’ll go to a bathroom in the dorm, or if I’m on campus, like a quiet floor of the library where nobody’s around. It’s just… I get really scared that all the food is just sitting there and it’s going to turn into weight, and I kind of panic. I know that’s probably not the right thing to do.
How often do these eating episodes happen?

I guess… more than I’d like to admit. It’s not every single day, but for most of this semester it’s been several times a week.

And usually if the eating happens, the throwing up happens too. I kept telling myself it was just stress or just a bad week, but looking back over the last few months, I don’t think there’s really been a week where it stopped completely. That sounds like a lot, doesn’t it?
Do you worry about gaining weight?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I know everyone probably worries about it a little, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m, like, obsessed or anything.

But if I have what seems like a decent day — I go to classes, get through stuff — and then I catch my reflection in a dorm window or something, I’ll start comparing myself to the guys around me. If my stomach or even my face looks bigger, it just… it feels like I messed everything up. Like I failed, not just with food but as a person.

And then I don’t really want anyone to see me. I know that sounds kind of extreme.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you try to make yourself throw up after eating?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m doing it for some, I don’t know, dramatic reason, but that’s honestly what’s going through my head.

After I eat like that, I get really scared that the food is just… sitting there, and that it’s going to turn into weight. So I’ll end up in a bathroom in the dorm, or sometimes somewhere quiet like a floor of the library, and make myself throw up. It’s mostly because I’m terrified of gaining weight. Does that… answer what you mean?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I don’t weigh myself in any kind of consistent way, so I don’t want to give you a number and be wrong.

I feel like my clothes fit kind of differently sometimes, but I also don’t know if that’s just me paying too much attention. So… I haven’t noticed a clear big change, I guess. Is that okay to say?
Do you think you would still try to make yourself throw up after eating even if you knew you weren't going to gain any weight?

I… I want to say no, because that sounds like the right answer. Like if I knew for sure I wouldn’t gain weight, maybe I wouldn’t need to.

But honestly, when it happens, that’s not how it feels in my head. After I eat like that, I get this panic that it’s just sitting there and turning into weight, and then I usually end up in the dorm bathroom, or somewhere quiet like a library floor, trying to throw it up.

So… I guess it’s really tied to that fear. If I truly believed I wouldn’t gain weight, maybe I wouldn’t, but I don’t know if I can actually believe that in the moment. Does that make sense?
Do you think your weight or body shape is abnormal even when others tell you that you look fine?

Yeah… sometimes. I mean, people will say I look fine, or normal, and I try to take that in, but it doesn’t really stick.

Like I can have an okay day in classes, and then I’ll catch my reflection in a dorm window or something, and if my stomach or my face looks bigger than the guys around me, it just… ruins everything. It feels like I failed somehow, even if nothing actually happened. And then I don’t really want anyone to see me.

I know that probably sounds kind of extreme. I’m not trying to be difficult, it’s just how it feels in the moment.
Do you think you would still be afraid of gaining weight if you were at a weight that most people would consider underweight?

I think… yeah, probably. I don’t like saying that because it sounds irrational, and I know you’re asking if being underweight would change it.

But I feel like even if people said I was too thin or whatever, I’d still find something that looked wrong. Like I can have a decent day in classes, and then I catch my reflection in a dorm window and suddenly my stomach or my face looks bigger than the guys around me, and it feels like I failed at everything. Then I just don’t want anyone to see me.

So… I think the fear would still be there. Is that what you mean?
